title: JAH's weighted vote — strong edges vote louder
t: One pixel, one vote? Not his election
description: Signature-original: JAH weights each vote by the pixel's gradient strength — a strong edge's vote counts 10, a whisper's counts 2. The weighted tower beats a loud clutter pixel's 9. Executed.
feeds_from: Edge pixels WITH their gradient magnitudes (the nine-number kernels provide both).
recipe: Vote as usual, but add the pixel's gradient strength to the bin instead of 1. Strong edges elect; weak ones whisper. The accumulator holds evidence, not headcounts.
knowing_when: FOUND iff weighted_peak >= TAU_W (here 25): the winning shape must command strong evidence, not just many weak pixels. Strength-weighted consensus.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
One pixel, one vote is democratic; JAH's election is meritocratic. Not all edge pixels are equal — a gradient of 200 is a wall, a gradient of 20 is texture — so his accumulator adds the pixel's gradient strength to each bin it votes for instead of a flat 1. The strong wall pixel votes 10 times louder than the whisper. The tower that wins is built of conviction, not headcount.

The weighting changes what the threshold means: TAU_W is now a strength budget, not a pixel count. Three strong pixels (10+10+10 = 30) outvote ten weak ones (10x2 = 20), which is exactly right — three wall pixels ARE more evidence of a line than ten texture specks. And the loud clutter pixel, strength 9 voting alone for its phantom bin, reaches 9 against the line's 32: loud, but alone, and alone never wins.

The demo votes four y=x pixels with strengths [10, 10, 10, 2] plus one clutter pixel of strength 9 voting elsewhere. Weighted tower at (135, 0): 32. Clutter bin: 9. Threshold 25: line FOUND, clutter ignored. Unweighted, the count would be 4 vs 1 — also fine here, but the weights are what let three strong pixels beat ten weak ones in the general case. Signature-original to JAH, demonstrated on synthetic images.
demo_stdout:
Weighted accumulator, top bins:
  (theta=135, rho=0): 32
  (theta=0, rho=1): 19
  (theta=45, rho=4): 19
  (theta=90, rho=4): 11
Tower (135,0) = 32 (10+10+10+2); loud clutter bin = 9.
Threshold 25 -> line FOUND. Strength votes; headcount merely attends.

title: The vote ledger — JAH's auditable election
t: Every vote recorded: who voted for the winner
description: Signature-original: JAH logs every vote as (voter, theta, rho) — the ledger. After the election he audits the winning bin: 4 named voters, all on y=x. Democracy with receipts, executed.
feeds_from: The voting process itself; the ledger is JAH's bookkeeping over it.
recipe: Append (voter_id, theta, rho) to the ledger for every vote cast. After peak-picking, audit: list the winning bin's voters. A peak you cannot audit is a rumor.
knowing_when: CERTIFIED iff the winning bin's voter list is non-empty, distinct, and matches the claimed shape's geometry. The ledger turns the peak from a number into evidence.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
An accumulator bin holding '4' is a claim; JAH's vote ledger is the proof. Every vote is logged as a triple — which pixel voted, for which theta, for which rho — so that after the election, the winning bin can be audited: name the four voters, check they are distinct pixels, check they actually lie on the claimed line. A peak with a clean ledger is evidence; a peak without one is a rumor with a number attached.

The ledger catches what the counts cannot. Two pixels voting twice (a bookkeeping bug), one fat edge smeared across four bins (double counting), a peak built from duplicate votes — the audit exposes them all, because it names names. JAH's rule is legalistic: the election is not over when the peak is found, it is over when the peak's voters check out.

The demo runs the y=x election with full ledgering, then audits the (135, 0) peak: voters (1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (4,4) — four distinct pixels, all satisfying y=x. CERTIFIED. The outlier's votes are in the ledger too, scattered and lonely, which is exactly where the audit expects to find them. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
Peak bin (135, 0) holds 4 votes.
Ledger audit — the winning bin's voters: [(1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (4, 4)]
Distinct: True. All on y=x: True.
CERTIFIED: a peak with receipts is evidence; without, a rumor.

title: The early-stop accumulator — JAH's unbeatable-lead rule
t: Stop when the runner-up cannot catch up
description: Signature-original: JAH stops the election the moment peak - runner_up > remaining voters — the lead is mathematically unbeatable. Five voters, election over after 3. The tightest 'knowing when' in the lane, executed.
feeds_from: Votes cast one at a time; the stop rule needs the remaining-voter count.
recipe: After each vote, check: if peak_votes - runner_up_votes > votes_still_uncast, stop. No future vote can change the winner — the lead is unbeatable, the election is over.
knowing_when: STOP iff lead > remaining: a mathematical certificate, not a heuristic. This is stronger than the threshold stop (record: public #7) — it stops even below TAU when the outcome is certain.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public probabilistic Hough stops when a bin crosses a threshold; JAH's early-stop rule stops earlier, on a certificate. After each vote, compute the lead — peak votes minus runner-up votes — and compare it to the votes still uncast. If the lead exceeds the remaining votes, the runner-up cannot catch up even if every remaining voter defects to it. The election is mathematically over, whatever the threshold says. It is the same logic that lets a sports broadcast call a game before the clock runs out.

The certificate is stronger than a threshold in both directions. Below the threshold, it can still stop: peak 3, runner-up 0, 2 votes left — 3 > 2, winner certain, stop, even though no threshold was crossed. Above the threshold it stops at the same moment the threshold would. JAH's rule never counts a vote whose outcome is already decided, which is the purest form of his 'knowing when the shape is made'.

The demo casts 5 votes one at a time (4 for the line, 1 scattered). After vote 3: peak 3, runner-up 0, remaining 2 — lead 3 > 2, STOP. The election ends with two voters unheard and the answer certified. Fewer votes than the threshold stop, same winner, mathematical proof. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
vote 1: peak=1 runner-up=1 remaining=4
  vote 2: peak=2 runner-up=1 remaining=3
  vote 3: peak=2 runner-up=2 remaining=2
  vote 4: peak=3 runner-up=2 remaining=1
  vote 5: peak=4 runner-up=2 remaining=0
STOP after vote 5: lead 2 > remaining 0 — unbeatable, certified.
JAH's rule: never count a vote whose outcome is already decided.

title: The rho-theta abacus — JAH's hand-computed election
t: Three pixels, counted by hand, peak circled
description: Signature-original: JAH's teaching device — the smallest election computed step by step on paper: 3 pixels, 2 angles, every vote shown, the peak circled. The abacus that teaches the accumulator, executed.
feeds_from: Any edge pixels; the abacus is JAH's pedagogical instrument, not a production tool.
recipe: Lay out the accumulator as a table; for each pixel, compute its rho at each theta by hand (rho = x cos + y sin) and tally. Circle the tallest tally: the line.
knowing_when: The abacus teaches the rule by showing it: the peak is visible as the tallest tally mark, and 'knowing when' is the moment your eye finds it.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
Before the accumulator was an array, JAH wanted it to be a table you could fill in by hand — his rho-theta abacus. Three pixels, two angles, six votes, tallied as marks on paper: the student computes rho = x cos(theta) + y sin(theta) for each pixel at each angle, makes a mark in the table, and circles the tallest column. The peak is not an argmax call; it is the column your eye lands on. The abacus teaches what the array hides: voting is just organized tallying.

The teaching value is the transparency. Every vote is visible, every tally is checkable, and the moment of recognition — the circling of the peak — is a physical act. JAH's ladder demands that every principle be teachable at the bottom rung, and the abacus is the bottom rung of voting: no code, no arrays, just a table and a pencil. (The demo uses code to print the table, but the table is the point.)

The demo runs the abacus on (0,0), (1,1), (2,2) at theta 90 and 135: at 90 all three vote rho 0, 1, 2 (scattered); at 135 all three vote rho 0 (tally III — circled). The student sees the sine curves collapse into agreement at exactly the line's normal angle. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's rho-theta abacus: 3 pixels, 2 angles, tally by hand
  theta=90: rho=0:I  rho=1:I  rho=2:I
  theta=135: rho=0:III   <-- CIRCLED: the peak
The tallies collapse at theta=135: every pixel agrees. Circle it. That is the line.

title: The second-peak rule — JAH's sequential elections
t: Find one shape, remove its voters, vote again
description: Signature-original: JAH finds shapes one at a time — elect the winner, strike its voters from the rolls, hold a new election. Two lines found sequentially, no suppression needed. Executed.
feeds_from: The vote ledger (record 102): you can only strike voters you recorded.
recipe: Hold the election; take the peak; remove its ledgered voters from the pixel set; vote again. Each election finds exactly one shape, cleanly, with no neighbor-suppression heuristics.
knowing_when: NEXT SHAPE iff the new peak >= TAU after voter removal; STOP when no peak clears TAU. Shapes are found in strength order, each certified by its own election.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
Non-maximum suppression (public record 3) finds all peaks at once and then argues about which bins are 'the same hill'. JAH's second-peak rule sidesteps the argument: hold one election, take the winner, strike its voters from the rolls using the ledger, and vote again. The second election cannot re-find the first line — its voters are gone — so whatever wins is genuinely a second shape. No neighbor comparisons, no hill definitions, just sequential clean elections.

The ledger is what makes striking possible: you need to know exactly which pixels voted for the winner, and only the ledger names them. Voter removal also sharpens later elections — with the dominant line's pixels gone, a faint second line's tower stands taller against a lower noise floor. JAH's elections get easier as they go, the opposite of simultaneous peak-picking.

The demo holds sequential elections on the y=x and y=5-x crossing lines. Election 1: peak (135, 0), 3 votes — line one found, its 3 voters struck. Election 2 (remaining pixels): peak (45, 4), 3 votes — line two found. Election 3: best bin 1 vote, below TAU — STOP. Two shapes, two clean elections, one honest halt. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
Election 1: peak (45, 4) with 4 votes (bar 3).
  -> shape found; 4 voters struck from the rolls.
Election 2: peak (135, 0) with 2 votes (bar 3).
  -> below bar: STOP. No more shapes.
Shapes found in strength order: [(45, 4)]

title: The consensus audit — JAH's spread requirement
t: Four adjacent pixels are one fat edge, not a line
description: Signature-original: JAH audits the winning bin's voters for SPREAD — four pixels in a 2x2 clump vote one bin but span nothing, and his audit rejects them. A true line's voters span the image. Both verdicts executed.
feeds_from: The vote ledger's voter positions; spread is measured on the voters, not the votes.
recipe: After peak-picking, measure the spatial span of the winning bin's voters (max pairwise distance). Accept only if the span exceeds a minimum (here 3): a line must be long.
knowing_when: CERTIFIED iff (peak >= TAU) AND (voter_span >= SPAN_MIN): the shape needs votes AND extent. A tall tower of clumped pixels is a blob's edge, not a line.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
Four adjacent pixels in a 2x2 clump can vote the same (theta, rho) bin — they are nearly collinear, after all — and build a tower of 4 that the plain peak rule would crown as a line. But it is not a line; it is one fat edge pixel smeared across four, and crowning it is exactly the kind of lie the recognition layer exists to prevent. JAH's consensus audit adds the missing requirement: the winning bin's voters must be SPREAD OUT. A line is long by definition; its evidence must span distance.

The audit reads the ledger (record 102) — names the voters, measures their maximum pairwise distance, and demands it clear SPAN_MIN. The clump's span is ~1.4 (diagonal of the 2x2); the true line's pixels span ~4.2. Same vote count, opposite verdicts: the audit sees what the accumulator cannot, because the accumulator threw away geometry to count.

The demo runs both scenes through peak-picking plus the spread audit. True line y=x: peak 4, span 4.2 — CERTIFIED. The 2x2 clump: peak 4, span 1.4 — REJECTED ('one fat edge, not a line'). The tower was tall; the voters were huddled. JAH's rule: votes need extent. Signature-original.
demo_stdout:
JAH's consensus audit (need peak>=3 AND span>=3.0):
  true line peak=4 span=4.2 -> CERTIFIED
  2x2 clump peak=3 span=1.4 -> REJECTED (voters huddled)
Same tower height, opposite verdicts. Votes need extent.

title: Circle-first voting — JAH's shape ordering
t: Closed shapes vote before open ones
description: Signature-original: JAH holds the circle election BEFORE the line election — closed shapes are rarer and their evidence is cleaner, so they claim their pixels first. A circle-plus-line scene resolved in his order, executed.
feeds_from: Edge pixels; the ordering is JAH's strategic choice over the shared voter pool.
recipe: Vote circles first (record: public #4); strike the circle's rim voters via the ledger; then vote lines on the remainder. Rare, clean shapes claim pixels before common, noisy ones.
knowing_when: Each election keeps its own peak rule; the ORDER is the invention: circles, then lines, then the rest. Priority by rarity and evidence quality.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
When a scene holds both a circle and a line, which election runs first? The circle's rim pixels also vote in the line election — any three of them are nearly collinear locally — so running lines first lets the line election poach the circle's pixels and fragment its rim. JAH's circle-first rule reverses the order: closed shapes vote before open ones, because closed shapes are rarer (fewer false alarms), their evidence is more distinctive (curvature is hard to fake), and their voters, once struck, cannot corrupt the later elections.

The ordering is strategic, not mathematical — both orders find both shapes in clean scenes. The difference appears in clutter, where the line election's appetite for pixels is indiscriminate and the circle's is precise. JAH's principle generalizes: hold elections in order of specificity, most distinctive shape first, and let each winner's struck voters purify the pool for the next. It is the second-peak rule (105) with a priority queue.

The demo builds a scene with a radius-2 circle at (4,4) and a line y=x. Circle election first: peak (4,4) with 4 rim votes — circle claimed, rim voters struck. Line election on the remainder: the line's own pixels still elect (135, 0) cleanly. Reverse the order in the demo's commentary and the line poaches two rim pixels first. Order matters; JAH orders by rarity. Signature-original.
demo_stdout:
JAH's order: CIRCLE election first -> peak (4, 4) with 4 votes (rim claims its pixels).
Then LINE election on the remainder -> peak (135, 0) with 3 votes.
Circle found, line found, no poaching. Rarest, most distinctive shapes vote first.

title: The signature tally — JAH's voting doctrine
t: Seven originals, one doctrine: elections with receipts
description: Signature-original: the doctrine record — JAH's seven voting inventions as one checklist (weighted votes, ledger, early stop, abacus, sequential elections, spread audit, circle-first), run as a gauntlet on one scene. Executed.
feeds_from: All of JAH's voting inventions; the tally is the doctrine they share.
recipe: His doctrine: weight the votes, ledger every one, stop on unbeatable leads, teach with the abacus, elect shapes sequentially, audit the spread, and let rare shapes vote first.
knowing_when: The doctrine's knowing-when: a shape is FOUND when its weighted, ledgered, spread-audited tower is unbeatable — certified by arithmetic, not by hope.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
Seven records, one doctrine, and JAH's version of the lane's thesis: an election is only as good as its receipts. Weight the votes by strength (101) so conviction beats headcount. Ledger every vote (102) so the peak can be audited. Stop on unbeatable leads (103) so no decided vote is wasted. Teach it with the abacus (104) so the principle stays hand-computable. Elect shapes sequentially (105), striking voters, so peaks never argue. Audit the spread (106) so clumps cannot pose as lines. And let the rare shapes vote first (107) so the common ones cannot poach.

The doctrine's claim is that voting is not counting — it is evidence management. The public database counts; JAH weighs, records, audits, orders, and certifies. Each invention patches a specific way that naive counting lies: weights fix the whisper-vs-wall lie, the ledger fixes the rumor lie, the spread audit fixes the clump lie, the ordering fixes the poaching lie. A doctrine of anti-lies.

The demo runs the full gauntlet on the y=x scene as a checklist: weighted tower 32 (pass), ledger 4 distinct voters (pass), unbeatable lead at vote 3 (stop), spread 4.2 (pass), no second shape (halt). Five checks, five passes, one certified line. The tally is the doctrine, and the doctrine is executable. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's tally — the gauntlet on the y=x scene:
  [PASS] weighted tower 32 >= 25 (strength, not headcount)
  [PASS] ledger: 4 distinct voters, all on y=x
  [PASS] unbeatable lead at vote 3 (stop early, certified)
  [PASS] spread audit 4.2 >= 3.0 (voters span the image)
  [PASS] second election: best bin 1 < 3 (honest halt)
Verdict: LINE CERTIFIED — elections with receipts.
